newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek depos/swaps softer, BoGr switches to o/n bid.
newsitem.headline: Greek depos/swaps softer, BoGr switches to o/n bid.

text.p: Greek interbank depos and swaps were softer about 10 basis points across the board in late dealing and the Bank of Greece switched to its overnight 12.40 percent bid intervention as the money market was long on cash.

Liquidity improved by the renewal of only a portion of maturing T-bills -- those issued in physical paper form. Maturing T-bills on December 18 in dematerialised-book-entry form were not renewed and funds stayed in the system.
Dealers said around 200 billion drachmas matured on Wednesday.
On Tuesday, Greece's central bank announced that it was cutting its discount and overdraft rates by 100 basis points, down to 16.5 and 25 percent respectively.
Also, effective January 1 it will lower the rate it pays commercial banks on interest-bearing reserves by 150 basis points to 11 percent.
"The drop in the rate the central bank pays interest bearing reserves renders forex more expensive and thus pushes swap bids lower," said a money dealer at a state bank.
"It looks like we'll stay long on liquidity until the auction of floaters December 27 if there are no drachma outflows related to ecu purchases," the dealer said.
Greece will auction 200 billion drachmas of FRNs and 100 billion of fixed-coupon bonds on December 27. Rate details have not been specified yet.
The mark was quoted at 158.45/50 drachmas from Wednesday's 158.360 fix, the dollar at 246.07/17 drachmas from 245.660 and the Ecu at 304.87/97 from 304.910 drachmas.
